title: platform-technical-sandpit-playflows-cookbook-draft
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a working draft of a compact, engineer-friendly deck and facilitator notes for running a "sandpit" style technical validation with platform teams during pilot/onramp. Goal is to short-circuit long procurement loops by giving platform engineers a safe, repeatable set of playflows that exercise: latency SLOs, fallback routing, quantization tradeoffs, and cost-measurement hooks.

Primary audience:
- Integration / Platform engineers at mid-market or enterprise prospects
- SEs and field engineers running the sandpit with customers
- Solutions engineers preparing minimal infra and demo scripts

How to use this doc:
- SE copies the deck slides and speaker notes sections into a 20–30 min workshop (hands-on, guided).
- Run 3 playflows (Baseline, Constrained, and Failover) in a sandbox VPC or demo cluster.
- Collect the metrics in the Post-run checklist and produce a 1-page outcome summary for CD/PO.

Slide outline (for a 12-slide condensed deck):
1) Title + objective (2 minute) - set expectations, timebox, success criteria
2) Quick architecture (1 slide) - hosted vs dedicated vs private variants and what we will provision in the sandpit
3) The three playflows at-a-glance (1 slide) - Baseline, Constrained, Failover
4) Baseline play (2 slides) - workload, model variant, request pattern, expected metrics
5) Constrained play (2 slides) - simulate limited capacity, test routing policy and quantization impact
6) Failover play (2 slides) - induce an availability event and validate graceful degradation
7) Measurement plan (1 slide) - metrics to capture, dashboards to open, token breakdown guidance
8) Post-run artifact checklist (1 slide) - logs, traces, latency histograms, cost snapshot
9) Next steps / contractual hooks (1 slide) - reserved capacity sizing, follow-up benchmarks

Speaker notes highlights (bulleted, informal):
- Kickoff: "We want to see what happens when your real traffic shape meets capacity constraints — not just the happy path."
- Emphasize what we control: model version, batch sizes, KV-cache warming, and routing policy.
- For field SE: after baseline, ask the platform engineer "what's acceptable latency 95/99 for your endpoint?" and write it down.
- When toggling quantization: capture output quality metric (simple sampling + fuzzy-match score) and before/after token-cost.

Detailed playflows (operational steps):
- Baseline playflow (30 min):
  1. Deploy a short-lived dedicated pool with 2x small GPUs (or use hosted test model).
  2. Run a 5 minute ramp of real-ish request shapes (mix short/long).
  3. Capture per-request latency, token counts, error rates, and token-cost.
  4. Warm KV cache with prefix queries, then run 3 cold-starts to show delta.
- Key success: 95th latency < target (agreed at kickoff), errors < 0.5%
- Notes to self: keep a canned corpus for deterministic comparisons.

- Constrained playflow (30 min):
  1. Reduce available GPU instances by 50% or introduce CPU-only fallback pool.
  2. Change routing policy to prefer lower-cost model variant under load.
  3. Observe latency tail, queuing effects, and serve-rate.
  4. Toggle quantization profile (e.g., int8 vs fp16) and run a short quality eval script.
- Key success: graceful latency increase, no correctness regressions above threshold
- Common friction: platform firewalls blocking fallback pool — validate networking ports upfront.

- Failover playflow (15–20 min):
  1. Simulate region outage or kill primary serving process.
  2. Verify smart routing triggers fallback to compatible variant/region and that API returns 200 with degraded metrics rather than 5xx.
  3. Check tracing for end-to-end span correlation.
- Key success: <1 minute to route, and functionally acceptable degraded responses.

Measurement checklist (post-run):
- Latency percentiles (p50, p95, p99) per-playflow and per-model variant
- Token cost breakdown (prompt vs completion) and total tokens/sec
- Error taxonomy (5xx, rate limit, model errors)
- Quality skim: sample outputs for semantic drift after quantization
- Trace IDs for representative slow requests

Artifacts SE should return to account team:
- Short outcome memo (1 paragraph): what we saw, recommended next step\n- CSV of latency and token-cost snapshots
- 3 sample request/response pairs for each playflow state
- Link to perf dashboard and full trace set

Open questions / risks to resolve (for this draft):
- Do we provide an automated script to provision a demo private cluster or rely on customer infra? (pro: speed; con: security ops approvals)
- What is our minimum viable quantization sanity test (automated fuzzy-match threshold)?
- Should SEs ship a small client-side tool to collect token-cost with request IDs to simplify costing recon?

Quickrun checklist (one-pager to stick to laptop):
- Pre-checks: SSH keys, VPC peering, quota, model versions uploaded, KMS key in place if using private demo
- During run: start perf generator, open dashboard, mark timestamps for scenario transitions
- Post-run: stop generators, export traces, snapshot dashboard, write memo

Reuse and distribution notes:
- This doc is intentionally terse so SEs can copy/paste slides and notes for a given account.
- Appendix area (not yet fleshed out): code snippets for perf generator, terraform snippets for quick cluster, sample evaluation script (python).

Next edits planned:
- Add a 1-page troubleshooting cheat sheet (networking, quotas, GPU OOMs)
- Attach artifacts: minimal terraform module and a verified perf generator binary/Container ID
- Create a lightweight rubric for "pilot success" that can slot into the account playbook

Notes to collaborators: 
- Ethan: can you prototype the perf-gen CLI and add a sample invocation?
- Priya: put together a 1-page slide that summarizes contractual asks (reserved capacity starter sizes + pricing delta)
- Liam: validate the KMS steps for private demo and add a quick checklist for legal/security approvals

Linked quick artifacts (to drop into final deck):
- short script: perf-gen --qps 30 --shape mix.json --duration 300
- sample fuzzy-match eval: eval_quality.py --baseline samples/baseline.json --candidate samples/q8.json

End of draft.

(Informal style retained — this is a living doc for quick iteration with SEs. Replace with polished deck when we have validated perf-gen and terraform module.)
